first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so a guarded onboarding-shortening test addresses the clearest shared bottleneck and can improve qualified revenue without immediately sacrificing price or lead quality. Verify the prior onboarding result and the competing pricing evidence because promotional pricing may lift acquisition while weakening sustainable downstream value.

final.rationale: Run a standard, guarded simplification experiment focused on restoring onboarding completion and activation. The verified onboarding record shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, indicating durable downstream value rather than merely top-of-funnel lift. This directly addresses both current declines. Do not use promotional pricing as the primary experiment: although it increased qualified revenue 18%, the 30-day retention decline of 12% and failure at the first renewal cycle make it unsuitable for sustainable qualified revenue. Monitor activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention with holdout safeguards.
